findings.evidence: Abstract: 'Of 78 items included in the consensus process, 38 reached consensus.' Results: 'Twenty-six items reached consensus in Round 1' + 'Eight items reached consensus in Round 2' = 34. Rebuilding Table 2 from the stored results/final/0.main_table.csv with the manuscript.Rmd create_summary_table rule gives consensus_final counts 1=28, 2=6, no=45, i.e. 34 of 78 items. 26+8=34, not 38. [Red (build_passport.py, archive_verified): the verification stage printed the authors' stored value with an executed check and upheld the conflict.]

The Abstract gives 38 ('...Of 78 items included in the consensus process, 38 reached consensus....'); the body never states 38. The body sentence about the same quantity (shared words: consensus, items, reached) gives 34: '...Consensus was reached for 34 items....'. Confirm that both refer to the same quantity (same cohort, test set, metric) before keeping it.

The paper defines a threshold of at least 70% ("### Definition of consensus Before launching the survey, the steering committee defined consensus as at least 70% of participants in each nonstudent stakeholder group rating an item as “essential” (i.e., between 7 and 9 "), but no comparison in the code uses 0.7; the code compares at 0.75 (`consensus = if_else(perc_essential >= 0.75, TRUE, FALSE),`). Check which threshold produced the reported results. Same pattern at 1 more place(s): Definition of consensus (p. 3) vs code/manuscript.Rmd:157.

The text reports an additional study or analysis: 'A follow-up survey of 46 heads of department in 2023 found that 31 of these 34 items were already taught at their institutions.'. Its head count 46 appears nowhere else in the paper, the phrase 'follow-up survey' is used in no other sentence (the Methods do not describe it), the sentence cites no source, and the code, README and file names in the materials do not contain the number. Look for its data, code, table or supplementary item; if there is none, the analysis cannot be checked from what was released.

'1. Our final sample comprised 113 participants who passed the attention chec': 113 participant(s) appears once, while 103 participant(s) appears 3 times (and 103 is used as a denominator elsewhere). A typo, or a different subgroup?

The paper reports a median absolute change ("Of the 47 items included in both Round 1 and Round 2, four went from not reaching consensus to reaching consensus, the median absolute change in the percentage of participants that rated an item as essential was 3.8%, an"), but the code computes mean(abs(...)) (`mean(abs(compare_rounds$perc_essential_compare))*100,`) (and 5 similar line(s)) and never median(abs(...)). The reported statistic may be mislabelled.
